details: jikaya-parser@1.0.0 contains no functional code — index.js is a single placeholder line (`console.log("parser for jikaya format")`) — and exists only to install a dependency from outside the npm registry. Its package.json declares `"marker-script-suffix-mapper": "hxxp://web[.]vitemaweed[.]fr:4873/marker-script-suffix-mapper/-/marker-script-suffix-mapper-1[.]0[.]18[.]tgz"`, a raw tarball URL fetched over plaintext HTTP from a non-npm private registry host (web[.]vitemaweed[.]fr:4873, the default Verdaccio port). Installing jikaya-parser therefore pulls and installs a third-party package body that the npm registry never received and never audited; that tarball can be modified or swapped by whoever controls the host at any time, and plaintext HTTP also lets a network attacker substitute the archive in transit. The package ships no lifecycle hooks, no bin entries and no other code, so its sole behaviour is this off-registry dependency stage.
